name: Shelter_Material_Properties
description: Insulation, durability, and weather resistance properties of building materials.

questions.question: Does choosing building materials teach real thermal conductivity and R-value concepts?
questions.answer: Yes. Materials display their R-value per unit thickness. Players learn that aerogel insulates better than regolith brick.

questions.question: Can players learn about specific heat capacity and thermal mass through shelter temperature management?
questions.answer: Yes. High-thermal-mass materials like stone buffer temperature swings. Players discover this through night-day comparisons.

questions.question: Does material durability under weather teach real material science concepts like weathering, spalling, and fatigue?
questions.answer: Yes. Freeze-thaw cycles crack porous materials. Thermal expansion fatigues joints. Players learn real degradation science.

questions.question: Can players experiment with composite materials (layered walls, reinforced panels) to discover emergent properties?
questions.answer: Yes. A metal skin over an insulating core gives both durability and thermal performance. Players discover this combination.

questions.question: Is realistic material simulation with scientific accuracy a unique selling point for the game?
questions.answer: Yes. No survival game simulates real material science. This is a distinct market differentiator.

questions.question: Do meaningful material choices create emergent player stories (my ice roof melted, my stone base survived the storm)?
questions.answer: Yes. Material failures create memorable emergent narratives that players share in forums and reviews.

questions.question: Does material variety across biomes drive exploration and replayability?
questions.answer: Yes. Rare materials in dangerous biomes incentivize exploration. Each playthrough uses different material combos.

questions.question: Can visible material degradation over time drive emotional attachment and maintenance gameplay?
questions.answer: Yes. Watching your carefully built shelter weather and age creates maintenance urgency and emotional investment.

questions.question: Do materials visually degrade, crack, discolor, and erode with prolonged weather exposure?
questions.answer: Yes. Visual degradation uses material-appropriate shader effects: rust on metal, spalling on stone, warping on wood.

questions.question: Do different materials (regolith, ice, metal, composite, organic) have visually distinct textures and shaders?
questions.answer: Yes. Each material family has unique albedo, roughness, normal maps, and subsurface scattering behavior.

questions.question: Can local materials be gathered from the environment based on biome geology?
questions.answer: Yes. Biome-specific resource nodes yield region-appropriate materials. Desert biomes yield sand-based composites; ice biomes yield ice blocks.

questions.question: Do rare or high-performance materials require exploration of dangerous or distant locations?
questions.answer: Yes. High-grade insulation ores exist only in deep caves. Aerogel precursors require extreme altitude collection.

questions.question: Can material property definitions be fully data-driven from JSON/CSV data tables?
questions.answer: Yes. Each material has a data table row: density, R-value, tensile strength, weather resistance, cost, weight.

questions.question: Is real-time insulation and thermal simulation cheap enough to run on the target RTX 3060?
questions.answer: Yes. Thermal simulation is a simplified finite-difference model per-shelter, computed every 30s. Negligible GPU cost.

questions.question: Can a basic material system (3 materials, R-value affecting temperature) be prototyped in one day?
questions.answer: Yes. Three materials with different R-values and a simple interior-temperature delta tick can be built in 4 hours.

questions.question: Do material states (mass, assigned module, degradation level) save and load correctly with the save game system?
questions.answer: Yes. Per-module material assignment and degradation percentage serialize to save game JSON.

questions.question: Does the game code generator need templates for material data asset classes and material instance components?
questions.answer: Yes. A UMaterialPropertiesDataAsset class and per-module dynamic material instance component need generator templates.

questions.question: Can material property interactions (thermal, structural, weather) be tested via automated sleepwalker sims?
questions.answer: Yes. Sleepwalker can build identical shelters with different materials, expose them to weather, and measure temperature/degradation differences.

questions.question: Is material degradation implementable as a simple damage-over-time tick with material-specific rates?
questions.answer: Yes. Each material defines (weather resistance, fatigue rate, repair cost). Degradation is time-exposure * weather-severity / resistance.

questions.question: Can material balance (cost vs. performance) be tuned entirely through data tables without code changes?
questions.answer: Yes. All material parameters live in data tables. Balance passes require no code recompilation.

questions.question: Does material temperature simulation depend on the planet temperature system being operational?
questions.answer: Yes. Ambient temperature from the planet system drives the delta that material insulation resists.

questions.question: Does this prove that educational mechanics (real material science) can coexist with fun survival gameplay?
questions.answer: Yes. Material choice becomes a meaningful gameplay decision with visible consequences, proving education and fun are compatible.

questions.question: Was this sub-feature derived from Shelter_Habitat question 2 (learning material properties through choice)?
questions.answer: Yes. Shelter_Habitat Q2 introduces material property education, which requires detailed property simulation to deliver.

questions.question: Does complex per-polygon material degradation conflict with the 30+ fps performance target?
questions.answer: Minor conflict. Full polygon-level weathering is expensive. Use vertex-annealed material parameter blending per module face.

questions.question: What domain knowledge is needed for accurate material property values in the simulation?
questions.answer: Published material science data for R-values, tensile strengths, and weathering rates of extraterrestrial-relevant materials.

questions.question: Does teaching real material science through gameplay serve the goal of becoming the most famous educational RPG?
questions.answer: Yes. Material science is a core STEM topic. Teaching it through survival gameplay directly advances the educational RPG vision.

questions.question: Can this feature be verified by sleepwalker beat tests?
